name: v0.22.1
body:
# oh-my-codex v0.22.1

## Summary

This patch release ships critical fixes for the omx question command when stdin is closed, adds readline close event handling for EOF detection, reapplies verified handoffs and safe drains after v0.22.0, accepts aliased Codex homes for external live pins, and addresses three Codex findings from the v0.22.0 release review.

## Fixed

- **ACCEPT ALIASED CODEX HOMES FOR EXTERNAL LIVE PINS (#3939):** Accept either spelling of the configured Codex home when validating live pin cache paths, enabling external Codex home links and symlinks to resolve correctly while maintaining no-follow traversal security. This fixes live pin resolution when Codex homes are aliased or redirected.
- **FIX EOF DETECTION FOR CLOSED STDIN IN OMX QUESTION --UI (#4048, #4046):** Replaced input stream listeners with readline close event for more reliable EOF detection when stdin is closed. Handle closed stdin in `omx question --ui` with proper error handling to prevent crashes when the command is invoked without stdin.
- **PRESERVE NON-FORCE DRAINS AND REQUIRE VERIFIED CODE HANDOFF (#4034):** Non-force team drains no longer interrupt in-flight worker Git operations, and worker code handoff to the leader requires verified evidence before integration. This change was held out of v0.22.0.
- **ADDRESS CODEX FINDINGS FROM v0.22.0 RELEASE REVIEW (#4047):** Fixes for issues identified in Codex review of release PR #4042. Herdr team shutdown now fails closed when workspace teardown fails, so team state and worktrees are preserved instead of removed while workers may still run. Scale-up honors a team's persisted Herdr launch mode, and startup readiness evidence is tracked per worker instead of leaking across concurrent startups.

## Compatibility

No breaking API changes. Release-coupled metadata (`package.json`, `package-lock.json`, Cargo workspace, and plugin metadata) all report `0.22.1` at the pinned source.

## Verification

- `npm ci` — passed; packages installed and lifecycle hooks completed.
- `npm run build` — passed.
- `npm test` — the local run did not complete, so no local result is claimed. The full CI suite passed on dev `108bea31` (the source of this release), [CI run 42458800471](https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo/oh-my-codex/actions/runs/42458800471).
- `npm run lint` — passed. No lint fixes required.
- `npm run check:no-unused` — passed. No unused imports or declarations.

## Contributors

Thanks to [@ev78394](https://github.com/ev78394) (#3939), [@shenyankm](https://github.com/shenyankm) (#4034), and [@Yeachan-Heo](https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo) for contributing to this release, and to [@iqdoctor](https://github.com/iqdoctor) for reporting #4043.

**Full Changelog**: [`v0.22.0...v0.22.1`](https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo/oh-my-codex/compare/v0.22.0...v0.22.1)

name: v0.22.0
body:
# oh-my-codex v0.22.0

## Summary

This minor release ships the Herdr team runtime backend Phase 2 with worker capacity management and task claim renewal, improves conflict handling in team operations to fail closed on Git conflicts, and adds session execution comparisons and regression gates for reliable task tracking during multi-agent workflows.

## Added

- **HERDR TEAM RUNTIME BACKEND PHASE 2 (#4006):** Implement the Herdr team runtime backend continuation, including native session pane coordination, detached-launch design notes, and improved tmux integration patterns. This solidifies the team runtime foundation with enhanced reliability and design clarity.
- **SESSION EXECUTION COMPARISONS AND REGRESSION GATES (#3915):** Add `omx session compare <baseline> <candidate>` command with `--fail-on-regression` flag to capture execution snapshots during session transitions, compare sessions against baselines, and gate further work when regressions are detected (exit 2 for regression, 3 for inconclusive). This enables robust regression detection during multi-agent workflows and task execution validation.

## Fixed
- **RESERVE WORKER CAPACITY, RENEW TASK CLAIMS, AND GATE DELIVERY COMPLETION (#4036):** Fix followup bounds, implement claim renewal, gate delivery success, close lease gaps, recover pending receipts, bound lease shutdown, surface renewal errors, and recognize terminal handoffs. Support system Bash and renewal on tool activity; fix scope root reactivation to delivery debt and renew leases despite heartbeat persistence failures. Reserve worker capacity before assignment and compare persisted assignment snapshots for validation.
- **FAIL CLOSED ON GIT CONFLICTS AND HAND OFF PERSISTED TASK CLAIMS (#4035):** Remove automatic conflict resolution strategies (-X theirs/-X ours), make conflicts visible and require manual resolution, preserve conflict state during integration retries, align task assignment protocol with leader's atomic preclaim, and expand conflict-scenario test coverage.

## Compatibility

No breaking API changes. Release-coupled metadata (`package.json`, `package-lock.json`, Cargo workspace, and plugin metadata) all report `0.22.0` at the pinned source.

## Verification

- PR #4042 CI: 64 checks passed (one transient macOS network failure in native build).
- Back-merge PR #4044 CI: 61 checks passed (one transient macOS network failure in native build).

## Contributors

Thanks to @salacoste for the Herdr team runtime backend Phase 2 (#4006), @shenyankm for conflict handling improvements (#4035, #4036), and @hiSandog for session execution comparisons and regression gates (#3915).

**Full Changelog**: [`v0.21.48...v0.22.0`](https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo/oh-my-codex/compare/v0.21.48...v0.22.0)

name: v0.21.48
body:
# oh-my-codex v0.21.48

## Summary

This patch release stores live Codex pins outside the plugin fingerprint root so live-pin writes no longer change the fingerprint Codex approved (#4010, fixes #3898), and removes role-based reasoning-effort defaults from role prompts (#4021), ensuring Vision stays extraction-only unless reassessment is justified.

## Fixed

- **LIVE PINS OUTSIDE CODEX PLUGIN FINGERPRINT ROOT (#4010, fixes #3898):** OMX wrote mutable live-pin files inside Codex's fingerprinted plugin-version directory, so every pin write changed the plugin fingerprint and Codex repeatedly invalidated hook approval. Live pins now live in `<cacheBase>/.omx-pins/<version>`, outside the fingerprint root, so pin writes no longer change the approved plugin fingerprint (reviewer: @iqdoctor; reporter: @AkiraLan).
- **ROLE-BASED REASONING-EFFORT DEFAULTS (#4020, #4021):** #4021 replaced fixed 'Default effort: low/medium' role defaults in seven role prompts (build-fixer, debugger, git-master, style-reviewer, team-executor, vision, writer) with task-based effort recommendations that preserve the leader's selected effort. Vision prompt is updated to make effort recommendations conditional: 'If reassessment is justified from task demands, remaining uncertainty, available proof, and resource limits, recommend a supported reasoning effort and briefly compare plausible alternatives without a role-based default; otherwise preserve extraction-only output.' This ensures all role prompts correctly defer to leader effort selection and documented success criteria.

## Compatibility

No breaking API changes. Release-coupled metadata was synchronized to `0.21.48` on dev by #4017. `package.json`, both root `package-lock.json` version entries, the Cargo workspace and six workspace crates, and plugin metadata all report `0.21.48` at the pinned source.

## Verification

- `npm run build` — passed.
- `npm test` — passed on the full test run: runtime build, all Node test files, generated catalog check, and prompt-inventory check completed.

- Release workflow [42416497142](https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo/oh-my-codex/actions/runs/42416497142) completed successfully with native builds for macOS arm64/x64, Linux x64, and portable bundles.

name: v6.9.0
body:
Image to PPTX gains OCR text evidence, text-removed bases, and checked image layers, and now runs on any vision host with an `image_gen.py` reference-image backend. Narration adds an OpenAI Realtime provider, `image_gen.py` can produce animated GIFs on OpenAI `gpt-image-2.6`, and a round of conversion and round-trip fixes stops sources from being overwritten or silently altered.

## Image to PPTX

- New `scripts/image_ocr.py`: `scan` OCRs normalized page images into reviewable text blocks (line boxes, estimated font size, sampled ink color), and the text layer becomes native text over a text-removed base. Removal results are composited back onto source pixels, and merged bases are checked for text left inside removal boxes (37efd014, e55a56ff, 574265a0, d1619e4f).
- New `scripts/image_layers.py`: `check` verifies an extracted layer is registered against the page, `diff-matte` derives a layer from the page's own pixels, `mono-matte` cuts a single-color graphic (such as a white logo) cleanly from a key plate, and merges are layer-aware and honour occlusion (bbc84447, 3c5cd655, 4a68cdda, 79d7cf57).
- The profile is no longer tied to one host: any vision host with a reference-image path works, either host-native editing or `image_gen.py --reference-image` (OpenAI, Gemini). Every page follows one assembly path; text removal defaults to `-b openai` and registered layers to `-b gemini`, with at most two residue retries before a page is marked for manual work (9577d604, 09547b1a, 7387d7b9, 6b0a2a5a, 8e809511).

## AI image generation

- `image_gen.py --gif-frames N [--gif-frame-ms MS]` returns an animated GIF from OpenAI `gpt-image-2.6-*`, for new images or to animate an existing one with `--reference-image`. Frame sizes are fitted to the server's sprite-sheet grids, which were measured on every frame count (db3bfc13).
- `gpt-image-2.6-*` models get the same size and quality handling as the 2.5 family (7c0eb65d).
- Each image is written once in its filename's format: a `.jpg` item keeps Gemini's JPEG bytes unchanged instead of a PNG round trip, and no orphan `.png` is left behind (8fe777ae).
- In manifest runs, rate limits go straight to the runner, which halves concurrency and honours `Retry-After` on the first 429 instead of after four backend retries. Successes are persisted from the worker thread, and each completion line reports the delivered pixels (9828c101, 54385b11, 650b5838, 946241c6).
- Sheet slicing respects sheets that carry their own transparency, source sheets are protected from being overwritten, and 16-bit grayscale images convert correctly (8db9dc57, 75e1fbf5, ce27cae0).
- New [AI Image Generation](https://github.com/hugohe3/ppt-master/blob/main/docs/image-generation.md) page records measured cost, size limits, text rendering, editing, and GIF behavior of the OpenAI and Gemini models (a99224bc).

## Narration

- `notes_to_audio.py --provider openai` uses `gpt-realtime-2.1-mini` over the Realtime WebSocket (the replacement OpenAI names for `tts-1` and `gpt-4o-mini-tts`, which retire on 2027-01-06). Each page confirms the effective session config before accepting audio. Recording-based custom voices work with `--voice-id voice_...` (ec4ca8bc, c67ca5fa, 4c449a11, 82468e8d).

## Edit Native PPTX round trip

- An export `-o` that points at the source or originally imported PPTX is refused before anything is written; previously it replaced the source, and later exports failed the source fingerprint (1d31b9ea).
- Edited native objects stay faithful on export (9b050352).

## Source conversion (source_to_md)

- Output paths that resolve or hardlink to an input are refused, so a pre-existing alias can no longer overwrite a source DOCX/XLSX; same-title web pages in one batch get distinct files (087cb942).
- PDF: soft masks, rotated table text, and table cell order are kept; header and footer bands are classified in displayed page coordinates (7d1fdd7c, 719786f2, 545e7fe9).
- DOCX and Pandoc: resource links, imports, and text stay faithful, and Pandoc includes resolve from the source with their media (21437a53, 1123e729). Charts keep their category context and literal Office text (fc627fee).

## Templates, icons, and the live preview editor

- Re-installing a template replaces its `Installed-from` line instead of stacking another (edc204a8).
- Each embedded icon instance gets its own internal IDs, so repeated icons no longer collide (1d35572c).
- The SVG editor keeps typed keys in form fields, shows raster data-URI images, and verifies that a running server is its own before reusing or stopping it (afad284d, afbfcd10).

## Community

- ModelGo joins as a corporate sponsor, and the README states that only the tool is free, not model tokens (f7fd3393, 263525c3, 2e8238a5, 9c39bf37).

完整更新内容 #### v6.4.3 - fix(server): restore unix-gated import dropped from resource route tests - fix(server): address audit findings in batch limits and export options - fix(web): parse maxScheduledExports as a number, align tauri cli pin - feat(release): add timetable-style download button SVGs - feat(release): add download buttons with badges to release notes
### 下载 | 包类型 | 平台 | 说明 | 文件 | |--------|------|------|------| | **一键安装包（推荐）** | Windows 7+ x64 | 内嵌完整运行环境，支持一键安装、自动登录与配置 | `QQChatExporter-Installer-v6.4.3.exe` | | **Shell 模式** | Windows x64 | 独立无头 (Headless) 运行环境，适合服务器或自动化部署 | `NapCat-QCE-Windows-x64-v6.4.3.zip` | | **Shell 模式** | Linux x64 | 独立无头 (Headless) 运行环境，适合服务器或 Docker 部署 | `NapCat-QCE-Linux-x64-v6.4.3.tar.gz` | | **Shell 模式（预览）** | macOS Apple Silicon (arm64) | 独立运行环境，首次启动会在本地生成一份专用的 QQ 运行副本，详见 [macOS 使用指南](https://shuakami.github.io/qq-chat-exporter/docs/macos-deploy.html) | `NapCat-QCE-macOS-arm64-v6.4.3.tar.gz` | | **Framework 模式** | Windows | 作为 QQNT 插件运行，与桌面端 QQ 共存 | `NapCat-Framework-QCE-v6.4.3.zip` | | **NapCat 插件商店包** | 跨平台 | 供已有 NapCat 环境的用户直接在插件商店安装 | `napcat-plugin-qce.zip` | > **版本选择指南** > - **一键安装包**：Windows 用户的首选。双击即可自动完成环境配置与登录（支持快捷登录或扫码），安装完毕后将自动唤起 WebUI 面板。 > - **Shell 模式**：独立运行版本，需单独进行 QQ 登录，适用于服务器环境部署及自动化备份需求。macOS 版本目前为预览支持，仅适用于 Apple Silicon（arm64）。 > - **Framework 模式**：作为 QQNT 插件运行，与当前使用的桌面端 QQ 共享登录状态，适合日常使用 Windows 桌面版 QQ 的用户。 > - **NapCat 插件商店包**：适用于已部署 NapCat 环境（含本地安装、Docker 或宿主机部署）的用户。请直接在 NapCat WebUI 的插件商店中搜索安装，**无需手动下载此压缩包**。
Shell 模式使用方法 **完整模式**（需登录 QQ，支持导出新增聊天记录）： - **Windows**：解压后双击运行 `launcher-user.bat` - **Linux**：终端运行 `./launcher-user.sh` - **macOS**：终端运行 `./launcher-user.sh`，详见 [macOS 使用指南](https://shuakami.github.io/qq-chat-exporter/docs/macos-deploy.html) **独立模式**（无需登录 QQ，仅用于浏览已导出的记录文件）： - **Windows**：双击运行 `start-standalone.bat` - **Linux**：终端运行 `./start-standalone.sh` - **macOS**：终端运行 `./start-standalone.sh` 启动后，请在浏览器中访问 `http://localhost:40653/qce`。若使用完整模式，需输入控制台输出的访问令牌 (Access Token) 进行验证。
Framework 模式使用方法 **方式 A：通过 `napiLoader.bat` 运行（推荐）** 此方式独立运行，无需预先安装 LiteLoaderQQNT。 1. 解压下载的 `NapCat-Framework-QCE-v6.4.3.zip` 文件 2. 确保当前已彻底退出正在运行的 QQ 客户端 3. 双击运行 `napiLoader.bat` 脚本 4. 若弹出 QQ 登录界面，请按常规方式完成登录 5. 在浏览器中访问 `http://localhost:40653/qce` **方式 B：通过 LiteLoaderQQNT 加载（仅限特定需求用户）** 此方式要求系统已配置好 LiteLoaderQQNT 环境。 1. 参照 [LiteLoaderQQNT 官方文档](https://liteloaderqqnt.github.io/) 完成前置框架的安装 2. 打开 QQ 设置，确认左侧菜单栏已出现 `LiteLoaderQQNT` 选项 3. 按照 LiteLoaderQQNT 或 NapCat 官方文档中的标准插件安装流程，将本插件部署至对应目录
如何找到访问令牌？ 按下 `Win + R` 键，输入 `%USERPROFILE%\.qq-chat-exporter` 并回车。打开该目录下的 `security.json` 文件，查找 `accessToken` 字段的值即可： ```json { "accessToken": "此处即为你的访问令牌", ... } ```
系统要求 需配合 QQ 客户端版本 34606 及以上使用（推荐版本 9.9.19-34740），[前往下载](https://im.qq.com/)。 - **Windows**：支持 Windows 10/11 x64。如运行报错提示缺少 DLL 文件，请安装 [Visual C++ 运行库](https://aka.ms/vs/17/release/vc_redist.x64.exe)。 - **Linux**：支持 Ubuntu 20.04+ / Debian 11+ / CentOS 8+。内置 使用静态 musl 构建，不要求特定 glibc 版本；QQ、NapCat 和注入模块仍需满足各自的系统依赖。 - **macOS**：⚠️ 预览支持，仅限 Apple Silicon（M1 及以上，arm64）。需已安装官方 macOS 版 QQ 与 Xcode 命令行工具（`xcode-select --install`，用于 `codesign`）。首次启动会在本地生成并签名一份专用的 QQ 运行副本，不会修改 `/Applications/QQ.app` 本体；该副本会失去系统 App 沙盒保护，仅用于后台运行 NapCat，详见 [macOS 使用指南](https://shuakami.github.io/qq-chat-exporter/docs/macos-deploy.html)。Intel（x64）Mac 暂未提供官方安装包。
> [!CAUTION] > 本项目完全免费且开源，遵循 GPL-3.0 开源协议。如果您是通过付费渠道获取的本软件，请立即申请退款并进行举报。 [使用文档](https://shuakami.github.io/qq-chat-exporter/) | [问题反馈](https://github.com/shuakami/qq-chat-exporter/issues) | [NapCat 项目](https://github.com/NapNeko/NapCatQQ) ### Contributors

name: v5.1.64
body:
**Desktop memory sync now starts as soon as the engine boots, without waiting for a session.** An engine started by `omo host ensure` loads extensions only when a session opens, while the desktop opens none until the engine has sent the memory-sync bootstrap handshake, so the two waited on each other. The compiled `omo` and the npm launcher now start that one claim before the engine loads whenever an RPC engine's launch declares a `memory-sync` channel; the first session reuses it. A claim that fails still reports memory sync as unavailable and never falls back to CLI credentials. ([#12702](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12702)) ([#12704](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12704))

Internal (tests only): macOS trust acquisition reads `/etc/ssl/cert.pem` through the already-injectable bundle reader, and a test now proves that a malformed default file yields the structured `openssl-default-file-malformed` drop entry (file, cause, block index, narrowing). ([#12633](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12633))

Internal (tests only): the OpenSSL default-file importer tests now pin that any high byte on a BEGIN line, not only a BOM, drops the whole file. ([#12632](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12632))

Internal (release tooling): the omo-native trust mutation harness counts a mutant as killed only when a named test fails by an assertion; a mutant that only throws a runtime error or crashes on load is now reported as `crashed` and fails the run. ([#12631](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12631))

### Fixed

- Memory sync no longer loses an edit when two devices change the same line of a memory file at the same time. Devices on this version keep both edits as whole lines, and every device converges. Before, the edits were merged character by character into text that matched neither (#12279).
  - Between devices on this version, an edit does not disturb a line nobody edited. The exception is a very large rewrite: when one device adds and removes more than about 2,000 lines of a note in one save, that save is merged character by character, as before this fix, so a concurrent edit to the same line can still splice.
  - When the note's body or the new text does not end with a newline, the edit is still merged character by character, as before, so two concurrent edits to that last line can still splice.
  - With a device that still runs an older version, its old character merge can still go wrong in these ways:
    - **Adjacent lines can fuse.** The older device rewrites the line right after a line this version edited. Depending on the two devices' internal ids, the two edits can fuse into one line followed by an empty line. Measured: from `head`, `one`, `two`, `tail`, this version writes `ONE` and the older device writes `TWO`, and the result can be `head`, `TWOONE`, an empty line, `tail`. Two older devices give `head`, `ONE`, `TWO`, `tail`.
    - **Leftover text moves.** The older device edits a line this version deletes. Its leftover text joins a neighbouring line.
    - **Its own diff touches other lines.** The older device's character merge crosses into a line its user did not edit. This also happens between two older devices.
  - Two older devices keep their old character merge until they update. ([#12597](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12597))
- Memory sync: the push phase of a large memory set no longer needs memory in proportion to the whole set. Every push step used to re-read and re-write one journal file holding every pending item's data, several times per batch. A device pushing a few thousand memory files therefore peaked at 2 GiB or more (#12286). The journal now keeps a small index of pending items with their data in separate files, and a push reads only the batch it is sending. Capturing the set before the push still holds each captured file's text until the capture ends. A journal written by an older build is converted the first time it is read, including one where an older build added items next to the new index. ([#12597](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12597))
- Memory sync: a device receiving a large memory set no longer slows down with every file it lands. The render step used to re-read every render record of the cycle for each file, so the first pull of a few thousand memory files took tens of minutes (#12285). Each file now costs the same, and the crash-resume behavior is unchanged. ([#12597](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12597))
- Memory git no longer takes `core.hooksPath`, `core.fsmonitor`, `include.path` or `includeIf.*.path` from an inherited `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` pair or `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS` entry, so an exported pair such as `core.hooksPath=/dev/null` can no longer silently skip the memory repository's hooks and mirror push. Every other injected pair (`url.*.insteadOf`, `http.extraHeader`, credentials, `safe.directory`, ...) still applies, renumbered; an injected list git itself cannot parse is dropped whole. Memory git also no longer inherits repository redirection (`GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_COMMON_DIR`, `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY`, `GIT_NAMESPACE`, `GIT_CONFIG`, ...), so it can no longer be pointed at another repository; `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` and `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM` are kept. ([#12360](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12360), fixes [#12354](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12354)) ([#12597](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12597))
- Memory sync no longer stops every push from a device when one memory file's change is larger than the 8 MiB batch limit: that file is held back and named in the sync status with what to do, every other memory keeps syncing, and the file syncs on its own once it fits. A change another device makes to a held file is kept and lands in this device's copy once the file fits, and a change an older build had already queued for such a file is recovered the same way instead of staying stuck. The TUI footer shows ` sync held` and the notice says the file is being held back, and a refused entry that pauses sync is never hidden behind a held file. ([#12284](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12284)) ([#12597](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12597))
- Opening a memory repository starts up to six fewer git processes: the local config defaults are read with one `git config --list` instead of one `git config --get` per key, and the line-ending repair is skipped while the repository tracks nothing. Every session that opens memory pays this, and on a loaded machine each git process costs hundreds of milliseconds. memory-core's own tests now run under the canonical 20 s test budget instead of per-file 5-15 s limits, which made them fail only on busy hosts. ([#12104](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12104), fixes [#12103](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12103)) ([#12597](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12597))
- `thread_send` no longer reports a message as `queued` when nothing will ever pick it up. When the target thread's session has no running drain, the send now answers `queued_offline`: the message is kept and the session takes it the next time it runs, so a caller knows no turn started and can act instead of waiting. The drain also reports a message it is holding behind the user's unsent draft, so a live drain is never mistaken for a missing one. ([#12488](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12488), fixes [#12486](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12486))
- Verify recursive removal (sync and async) actually removed its path, retry bounded silent leftovers, and join sweep-test removers before deleting their fixture parents. ([#11834](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11834))

### Added

- Windows releases now carry `omo-git-job-helper.exe`, a small native helper that runs each memory git command inside its own kill-on-close job object, so a later writer can prove that a killed writer's git is gone before it reclaims a stranded lock. Nothing uses the helper yet: memory-core keeps today's Windows behavior until a follow-up wires it in, and no release claims the new protocol until its in-flight-creation stress row has passed on Windows CI. ([#12105](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12105), part of [#10391](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10391)) ([#12597](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12597))

name: v0.6.10
body:
## [0.6.10] — 2026-11-08

Seventy-one merged pull requests since 0.6.9 (#433 to #570). What a user sees (each entry below states its own measurement and its floors):
- More complete answers: on our fixed in-sample questions (the same 163 everyday, 39 multi-file and 56 large-repository questions, commands and grader as the README answers table, one call each, no cache), everyday answers complete 129 → 132 of 163 (27 partial, 4 none), multi-file 12 → 19 of 39, large repositories 23 → 30 of 56; required items delivered 1,142 → 1,152, 84 → 114 and 148 → 164; no everyday answer stated something wrong (read in source). Answers are larger: everyday answers total 2.37 MB against 1.95 MB (median 10.7 KB against 10.6 KB), multi-file 722 KB against 536 KB, large repositories 1.97 MB against 1.38 MB, so bytes per complete answer rise from 15.1 to 18.0 KB (everyday) and from 60 to 66 KB (large repositories). One everyday question that read complete in 0.6.9 reads none in 0.6.10 (textual-09; hono-17 stays complete under the rule for exports flagged as public API; the README footnote says why). A grader input lost in a cleanup was restored (GRADER-FIX-1107), so the 0.6.9 and 0.6.10 columns are graded by the same scripts. In-sample questions, so progress between releases, not held-out performance; measured on main just before #570 (the `--for` anchor-choice change), which these figures do not include.
- Faster and lighter, as percent changes (each figure is that pull request's own measurement against the build just before it, on one machine; the changes were not measured together, and absolute seconds and megabytes come with the 0.7.0 table, measured on one other machine):
  - Warm `--deps` and `--for` on large trees use 35 to 67 % less CPU: vscode `--deps` -67 %, cockroach `--for` -57 %, envoy `--deps` -35 % (#542); a warm TypeScript `--deps` uses a further 22 % less CPU on vscode (#554). Cold runs gain less: instructions -14 % on vscode, -12 % on cockroach, -4 % on envoy.
  - Peak memory: on macOS the peak footprint of an index is about halved, -49 % on envoy, -47 % on cockroach, -48 % on vscode (#497); a warm run's peak is 30 to 40 % lower (-37 % on envoy, -40 % on terraform, -36 % on cpython) and sits at or under the cold run's (#556); the include closure of a large tree is held in an eighth of the memory, vscode's 32.5 MB of sorted vectors becoming 3.74 MB (-88 %, #505).
  - A file the nesting guard refuses no longer makes every warm run rewrite the whole cache: on envoy a 146 MB write per run is gone (#553; user CPU about 10 % lower, inside that measurement's noise).
- Fewer false edges and more honest answers: `--arch`, `--deps`, `--cochange`, `--impact` and `--export=cc.json` stop reporting coupling from edges the index never had; `--deps` stops calling every deep graph `tangled`; a "not found" from an index the memory guard cut no longer reads as proof of absence; `unused` is printed only when the scan can prove it; a `--path` chain stitched from calls bound by name alone is no longer printed as the plain answer; a Rust prelude call, a macro with no in-tree binding, and a Python call to a builtin or third-party name no longer bind a same-named definition; `--for` reads `confidence="high"` on a name-exact route only when the anchor heads the rows, and hedges a second-hop caller reached only by name.
- `--for` reaches more of what a task needs: registration rows and the registry key to what is registered under it (Python signals, TypeScript providers, computed-key registrars and their readers); the sites of a literal, a `--flag` and its default, a table or registration identifier; the family of an add-a-new-X task and the manifest lines that list a file; the doc sections for a prose question about the docs; re-export hops, alias chains and namespace re-exports; both sides of a missing `path from A to B`; the callers of the one function a sentence asks about; the implementations that can run at an interface call; the match arm that holds a literal; the one namesake a path word picks, while a test-only anchor among several no longer commits the route; Cargo `[[bin]]` and package.json `bin` / `main` entries; and `<syms>`, the shown files' other symbols.
- New and changed verbs: `--path` and `--connect` hops print the call site, the call and the callee's signature; `--impact` sums up the importers a cut listing hides and `--impact=<path>` lists a file's importers; `--defs` prints an alias's target and `--uses` lists the sites written through an alias; reST and Sphinx documents become real units and `--recall` serves the best-matching part of an HTML page; `ripwire wrap claude` routes edits through a ranged Read and Claude Code's native Edit.
- Language specifics: C++ pointers to member functions, `using` and namespace aliases and function-pointer typedefs; C / C++ quote includes resolve at the include roots a build passes; Rust `crate::`, `super::`, `self::` and `mod x;` resolve in the includer's own crate; Python `import a.b as c`, `from`-imported submodule calls and src layouts; TS/JS `run=` runs from the package directory.
- Contributors: a committed filename can no longer be read as commit metadata in `git log` framing (@pt-act, #433, #469); a TS/JS test in a subdirectory package gets a runnable `run=` hint (@llvm-x86, with @rainhuang0220's #330: #335, #442) and `--for` shows a Cargo `[[bin]]` and a package.json `bin` / `main` entry (@llvm-x86: #459, #460, folded into #511); langfacts slice 6c, Windows warm runs that leave the cache directory's ACL alone and shell test scripts named `test-*.sh` read as tests (@lennix1337: #471, #468, #496); an aliased Python `import a.b as c` is a file edge again, and C / C++ include roots with the foreign-qualifier veto (@jflowers: #530, #524, #526, #478); the installer hardening list of #293 (@s0undt3ch: #482); reports that led to fixes: reST and Sphinx documents (@muayyad-alsadi, #409), `--for` on a file name (@pguerrerolinares, #466), the router skill's language list (@gucliti, #521).
- Upgrade: caches rebuild once (`kParserVer` 301, `kCacheVersion` 49); quality snapshots of the older scheme are not used (scheme 25).
- Thanks: @pt-act (#433, #469), @llvm-x86 (#442, #459, #460), @lennix1337 (#436, #447, #471, #472), @jflowers (#478, #524, #526, #530), @s0undt3ch (#293), @muayyad-alsadi (#409), @pguerrerolinares (#466), @gucliti (#521) and @rainhuang0220 (#330).

---

Every entry of this release, with its measurement and its floors, is in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/redhat-et/ripwire/blob/ac869640e5be4548299852c66167a46c4e69746a/CHANGELOG.md).


## What's Changed
* Train 41b: C/C++ member-function pointers and struct-field slots join field calls by @joyful-ii-V-I in https://github.com/redhat-et/ripwire/pull/465
* README: answer quality by release (0.6.5 to 0.6.9) by @joyful-ii-V-I in https://github.com/redhat-et/ripwire/pull/467

* gitmine: a committed filename can no longer be read as commit metadata (#433 by @pt-act) by @joyful-ii-V-I in https://github.com/redhat-et/ripwire/pull/469
* gitmine: a committed filename can no longer be read as commit metadata (`git log` framing) by @pt-act in https://github.com/redhat-et/ripwire/pull/433
* README: move the Trendshift badge up under the tagline by @joyful-ii-V-I in https://github.com/redhat-et/ripwire/pull/474
* README: release-progress table moves into Measured; four size rows by @joyful-ii-V-I in https://github.com/redhat-et/ripwire/pull/475

* fix(test-gate): a TS/JS test in a subdirectory package gets a runnable run= hint (#335) by @llvm-x86 in https://github.com/redhat-et/ripwire/pull/442
* Train 42b: smart-pointer receivers, re-export hops and literal sites in --for, Claude Code edit route by @joyful-ii-V-I in https://github.com/redhat-et/ripwire/pull/476
* test-gate: the #330 default-include check, a subshell run= and the #442 follow-ups by @joyful-ii-V-I in https://github.com/redhat-et/ripwire/pull/480
* Train 43a: honest --path chains and file subjects in --for by @joyful-ii-V-I in https://github.com/redhat-et/ripwire/pull/481
* fix(install): harden skills/install.sh with the installer list from #293 by @joyful-ii-V-I in https://github.com/redhat-et/ripwire/pull/482
* Train 43b: registries, dotted-string imports, base-class hooks and declarations in --for by @joyful-ii-V-I in https://github.com/redhat-et/ripwire/pull/483
* Train 44: Python import edges, honest coupling without file edges, and more --for literal anchors by @joyful-ii-V-I in https://github.com/redhat-et/ripwire/pull/485
* langfacts: slice 6c per-language receiver and comment columns (Fixes #447) by @lennix1337 in https://github.com/redhat-et/ripwire/pull/471
* docs(contributing): refresh the common-code map, add slices #487-#490 by @joyful-ii-V-I in https://github.com/redhat-et/ripwire/pull/491
* isTestPath: read shell test-*.sh / *-test.sh and .e2e-spec. / .perf-spec. as tests (lands the filter part of #472) by @joyful-ii-V-I in https://github.com/redhat-et/ripwire/pull/496
* UNUSED-IN-FILE: --for unused cue on a file carries a per-def verdict table by @joyful-ii-V-I in https://github.com/redhat-et/ripwire/pull/503
* SUBJECT-ANCHOR: --for anchors the symbol a subject names by @joyful-ii-V-I in https://github.com/redhat-et/ripwire/pull/502
* Merging main stops conflicting on the gate list and generated counts by @joyful-ii-V-I in https://github.com/redhat-et/ripwire/pull/508
* TABLE-CONST: --for on a table or registration task reaches the identifier's table rows by @joyful-ii-V-I in https://github.com/redhat-et/ripwire/pull/507
* RULE3-MEMBER-GUARD: Rust/Python Rule 3 calls need a written binding to read as proven by @joyful-ii-V-I in https://github.com/redhat-et/ripwire/pull/504
* ep-manifest: Cargo.toml [[bin]] and package.json bin/main on --for (fold of #459 + #460, @llvm-x86) by @joyful-ii-V-I in https://github.com/redhat-et/ripwire/pull/511
* feat(ep-manifest): Cargo.toml [[bin]] on --for (fixes #450) by @llvm-x86 in https://github.com/redhat-et/ripwire/pull/459
* feat(ep-manifest): package.json bin/main on --for (#451) by @llvm-x86 in https://github.com/redhat-et/ripwire/pull/460
* recall: hand-written reference pages stop being demoted as generated by @joyful-ii-V-I in https://github.com/redhat-et/ripwire/pull/510
* history: bound the git walks and stop hanging on blobless clones by @joyful-ii-V-I in https://github.com/redhat-et/ripwire/pull/498
* deps/impact: four false claims fixed (shape, Rust mod containment, path selector, rollup) by @joyful-ii-V-I in https://github.com/redhat-et/ripwire/pull/509
* --for: TS/JS namespace re-exports, a proven qualifier, and a fallback ladder for an unresolved name by @joyful-ii-V-I in https://github.com/redhat-et/ripwire/pull/512
* Generated docs: published totals come from one dated snapshot, so open PRs stop conflicting on them by @joyful-ii-V-I in https://github.com/redhat-et/ripwire/pull/514
* FILE-GRAPH-CSR: flat file graph and a hybrid closure store built by an SCC fold by @joyful-ii-V-I in https://github.com/redhat-et/ripwire/pull/505
* DOCS-REST: reST and Sphinx documents become real units (#409) by @joyful-ii-V-I in https://github.com/redhat-et/ripwire/pull/506
* SHORT-KEY-SENTENCE: the <shortkey> ladder for one unresolved code-shaped name inside a sentence by @joyful-ii-V-I in https://github.com/redhat-et/ripwire/pull/517

* --for file tail walks the file page's first 160 rows, not 40 (FOR-TAIL-WIDE) by @joyful-ii-V-I in https://github.com/redhat-et/ripwire/pull/536

* perf(resolve): one normalization per TS probe list, a per-build (directory, specifier) memo by @joyful-ii-V-I in https://github.com/redhat-et/ripwire/pull/554

* for: confidence reads high on a name-exact route only when the anchor heads the rows (FRAME-HIGH-CONFIDENCE) by @joyful-ii-V-I in https://github.com/redhat-et/ripwire/pull/568

## Install

### Windows

#### Zip

2. Run the MSI
3. Run `nvim.exe` in your terminal

Note: On Windows "Server" you may need to [install `vcruntime*.dll`](https://neovim.io/doc/install/#windows).

### macOS (x86_64)

1. Download **nvim-macos-x86_64.tar.gz**
2. Run `xattr -c ./nvim-macos-x86_64.tar.gz` (to avoid "unknown developer" warning)
3. Extract: `tar xzvf nvim-macos-x86_64.tar.gz`
4. Run `./nvim-macos-x86_64/bin/nvim`

### macOS (arm64)

1. Download **nvim-macos-arm64.tar.gz**

### Linux (x86_64)

If your system does not have the required glibc version, try the (unsupported) [builds for older glibc](https://github.com/neovim/neovim-releases).

name: v15.12.0
body:
## Images are kept by default and show in My Work

- **Kept by default:** screenshots and images your agent reads or makes are now kept and linked to the observations from that turn, without sending them to an AI model. Image inference stays off (#5426).
- **"Keep images" switch:** the memory viewer's Settings has a new **Images** section. Turning **Keep images** off stops keeping new images; images already kept stay. A `"false"` you saved yourself is respected (#5426).
- **Gallery in My Work:** request cards show an image count and the first four thumbnails; the request drawer shows every linked image; any thumbnail opens a full-size gallery with keyboard navigation (#5427).
- **Fresh databases:** My Work lists observation activity again on a newly created database (#5427).
- **Local conversion you can rely on:** captured screenshots now convert on your own computer instead of failing as busy or timing out. Conversions wait their turn and get 20 seconds each, and every stored copy is lossy WebP so it stays small (#5431).
- **Cloud quota:** each owner can store up to 25 GiB of images on cmem.ai, the same limit Pro enforces (#5467).

## Fixes

- **Sessions:** after you delete a session in the viewer, new work in the same resumed conversation is captured again (#5463).
- **Sessions:** committed transcript entries are no longer replayed after a worker restart (#5321, thanks @lamimiahmed45-droid).
- **Hooks:** Grok Build's camelCase hook payload is accepted (#4282, thanks @nathan-v).
- **Hooks:** PreToolUse memory lookups are scoped to the current platform, so one harness no longer gets another's observations (#5008, thanks @SuperMarioYL).
- **My Work:** the scheduled refresh stays on the configured agent instead of falling back to another one (#5245, thanks @Dev-0710).
- **Claude CLI:** the Claude CLI is found again when `CLAUDE_CODE_PATH` changes (#5460, thanks @WhitePepperLambSoup).
- **Security:** `CLAUDE_MEM_DATA_DIR` and `CLAUDE_MEM_WORKER_HOST` can no longer be changed through `POST /api/settings`, and an OpenClaw reinstall keeps every existing setting (#5147, thanks @Wenjix).
- **Settings:** the Grok Bot awareness pilot agent IDs are no longer shipped as defaults (#4970, thanks @zichen0116).
- **Sync:** a backlogged sync drains instead of stalling, and `projection_busy` replies carry `Retry-After` (#3488).
- **Sync hub:** fewer Durable Object row writes per request (#4424, thanks @necatisozer) and no re-serializing of a page per operation when counting its bytes (#4937, thanks @devkancheti4-design).

## Also in this release

- **My Work:** leads with what's moving, groups cards by state and animates live changes (#5365).
- **My Work:** text is written in the owner's language, with an opt-in language setting (#5156, thanks @mehmetcelik7).
- **Interface:** opt-in Simplified Chinese for the worker interfaces (#5325, thanks @h6rime).
- **Observer health:** clearer SessionStart quota notices (#5134).
- **Installer:** the optional email and "how can we help" question is back, asked once in an interactive terminal only; sign-in is only for CMEM Pro (#5218).
- **Claude app plugin:** renamed to `cmem-pro`, carries the cmem.ai connector, and no longer captures memory lookups back into memory (#4570).
- **Providers:** cheapaimodel (#5158, thanks @nicho810) and Obscurify.ai (#5165, thanks @tonydavis629) presets for the OpenAI-compatible provider.
- **Smart read:** Delphi/Pascal support (#4953, thanks @nm3xyz).
- **Skills:** new community-sweep skill (#4374); oh-my-issues starts its cluster pass blind and adds an open-PR pass (#3617); the version-bump skill refuses to run outside thedotmack/claude-mem (#4575, thanks @somil14).
- **Docs:** the README says the observer trial goes through a payment-method checkout (#5087, thanks @Iyanuoluwa007).

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem/compare/v15.11.1...v15.12.0

body:

Stable releases remain on the `latest` dist-tag.

* test: add integration test coverage and fix KuzuDB fork crashes by @magyargergo in https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/209

name: graphify 0.9.104
body:
## graphify 0.9.104

- Security: **skill** the `/graphify` runbook no longer substitutes the scan path into Python code. Every generated code block (detect, AST and semantic extraction, build, diagnose, label, manifest, and `--update`) now reads the resolved scan root from the trusted `graphify-out/.graphify_root` sidecar that Step 1 writes through a quoted heredoc, instead of pasting the agent-supplied path into a string literal. A directory whose name carried a quote or `$(...)` could previously break out of `Path('INPUT_PATH')` and run as code; it is now read as inert data. Covers the assembled hosts and the Aider/Devin monoliths (#4762, thanks @danikdanik).
- Fix: **solidity** a call on a receiver of a contract or interface type (`IERC20 token; token.transfer()`, `IERC20(a).transfer()`, `token().balanceOf()`) binds by name and arity through that type's linearization to the type's own declaration, instead of producing no edge; gated to a single visible contract/interface and fail-closed on an unknown or ambiguous type (#5060, thanks @rohit-jsfreaky).
- Fix: **solidity** a call attached by a `using A for T` directive (`using SafeCast for uint256; x.toUint48()`) binds to the library or free function it attaches, matched by the receiver's type and an arity one greater than the call; fail-closed when the receiver type is unknown, the library is ambiguous, or two functions fit (#5062, thanks @rohit-jsfreaky).
- Fix: **solidity** members, free functions and types in one scope whose names differ only by a leading `_` or by case (`_grantRole` / `grantRole`) get separate node ids, so the `_` symbol no longer vanishes into its twin and its calls land on the right node (#5027, thanks @rohit-jsfreaky).
- Fix: **csharp** a constructor (instance, static or primary) is its own node owned by its type, with its body and `: base(...)`/`: this(...)` calls credited to it; `new X(...)`, `: base(...)` and `: this(...)` additively link the arity-correct overload, and two fitting overloads or an unresolved base give no constructor edge (#5054, thanks @rohit-jsfreaky).
- Fix: **csharp** calls inside a property or indexer accessor, an expression body, or an operator/conversion body are credited to that member instead of being lost; an indexer becomes a `this[]` node and an operator a `.operator +()` node (#5056, thanks @rohit-jsfreaky).
- Fix: **query** a same-label node that is the only match for a query term is kept as a seed instead of being dropped by the per-label cap, so every distinct term keeps at least one seed while generic-label flooding stays capped (#5027, thanks @Vaibhav2824).
- Fix: **watch** read-only events are kept out of the inotify mask via a change-only `event_filter`, so a large tree no longer drives watchdog into a self-sustaining queue-overflow loop; falls back with a warning on watchdog versions without `event_filter` support (#5033, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah).
- Fix: **cache** the `\\?\` long-path spelling is kept out of cache identity, so the same file reached through `\\?\C:\...` and `C:\...` shares one entry; also fixes empty stat-index writes under UNC shares, a spurious "stat index switched" warning on Windows, and a junction/symlink alias wrongly sharing its target's digest (#5035, thanks @Bortlesboat).
- Fix: **cache** stat-index keys stay root-relative under a Windows long-path root, so a moved or cloned corpus keeps the portable-key fastpath (#5035, thanks @Vaibhav2824).
- Fix: **tests** the TypeScript unicode fixture is written as UTF-8 on every platform, so byte offsets match the extractor on Windows (cp1252) hosts (#5064, thanks @ayushcodes10).
- Fix: **tests** the hook-freshness source mock is normalized through `os_long_path`, so the read-error/stale branch is actually exercised on Windows (#5065, thanks @ayushcodes10).
- Fix: **tests** the watch pending-queue test compares `Path` objects so `/` and `\` separators compare equal on Windows (#5039, thanks @Yi-111-a).
- Fix: **extract** an ambiguous Python import's placeholder node id is hashed from checkout-independent data (module name, scan-root-relative source file, location) instead of the absolute path, so the same project at a different path or a moved cache gets the same ids (#5045, thanks @Fardin7798).
- Fix: **yaml** a template using CloudFormation intrinsic tags (`!Ref`, `!GetAtt`, `!Sub`) no longer fails to parse: a scoped permissive loader rebuilds each `!`-tagged node's shape without evaluating it, while `!!python/...` tags still raise and never execute (#5077, thanks @ayushcodes10).
- Fix: **watch** a `--watch` incremental update rebuilds the full corpus when `graph.json` is missing, instead of writing a partial graph from the manifest alone (#5020, thanks @azizur100389).
- Fix: **watch** a change to a JS/TS resolution input (`tsconfig.json`, `jsconfig.json`, a lockfile) triggers a full rebuild so importers pick up the new resolution, instead of leaving stale `imports_from` edges (#5020, thanks @azizur100389).
- Fix: **ingest** two concurrent `graphify add` captures for the same URL no longer clobber each other: the capture file is created exclusively (`O_EXCL`) and a collision retries a fresh name, with the payload fetched once (#5020, thanks @azizur100389).
- Fix: **reflect** a malformed entry in the learning overlay is skipped instead of crashing the whole load, and a legacy null-source entry is preserved as a source-less annotation (#5020, thanks @azizur100389).
- Fix: **global** a malformed repo entry in the global manifest is dropped on its own, keeping the other tracked repos, and only a non-object root or repos map is backed up and reset (#5020, thanks @azizur100389).
- Fix: **query** a graph freshly built on a subfolder is no longer flagged as a pre-#1504 build (which nagged a no-op `extract --force`): the legacy-id probe strips the `.graphify_root` offset before deriving file stems, and a genuine legacy graph is still caught (#5019, thanks @neumannpeter1231-lang).
- Fix: **tree** `graphify export tree` recognises the `src` node alias (and `file`/`path`/`filepath`) so a graph carrying those keys renders a populated tree instead of an empty one; a concept-only graph still reports empty (#5030, thanks @Adityakk9031).
- Fix: **cli** `graphify provider add` accepts `--pricing-input=VALUE`/`--pricing-output=VALUE` equals-syntax and rejects a non-numeric, non-finite or negative price with a clean error instead of a traceback or a poisoned cost estimate (#5031, thanks @Adityakk9031).

The AST cache schema is bumped to 40; warm caches re-run the affected Solidity and C# extractions. The Python and YAML fixes above need no bump (placeholder ids are resolved after the per-file cache, and previously-failing YAML was never cached).

name: Skill 4.8.1
body:
- **The Stop hook asks less.** Findings stay listed, and the agent fixes or skips each one with a short reason. It asks you only when it cannot decide.

- **A design hook for Hermes Agent.** Hermes checks every file it writes and runs the end-of-session review before it finishes. Enable it once with `hermes plugins enable impeccable-design-hook`. Thanks to @kal-hermes for asking.

- **Hooks that stay wired.** `hooks status` shows each harness's real wiring, and `context` restores missing entries once you have accepted the hook. A user install follows `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, and cleanup no longer removes working project hooks. The hook stops re-reporting findings you did not touch (thanks to @provatic), VS Code Copilot hooks run under Windows PowerShell (thanks to @PhillyUrbs), and resuming a session no longer bloats the env file (thanks to @EnderWolf50).

- **Remove an element in live mode.** A Remove badge on a picked element, or Delete on an empty prompt, hides it, offers Undo, and stages the removal for Apply like a copy edit.

- **Live mode fixes.** Vue variants mount and keep their CSS, and Svelte and Vue previews wait for the compiled component instead of showing raw template. Tune edits survive the remaining variants arriving, the Apply repair choice survives a reload, and Rollback resets the dock (thanks to @ArmirKS for all three). Small elements pick their nearest pickable parent, captures keep self-hosted fonts, and the Nuxt plugin passes strict typecheck (thanks to @NarHakobyan).

- **Fewer false alarms.** URL scans wait out brand intros and judge contrast on the ground a reader sees, under scrims, dot grids and hover effects parked off the button. Faint decorative words are advisory. A `background` shorthand takes its colour from its final layer (thanks to @luckystar2026), and directory scans include `.mjs` and `.cjs` files (thanks to @Mercury-nju).

- **Fixes.** A harness you pick interactively installs even when another is already installed (thanks to @Minayuki523). `check` no longer reports updates on every Windows install (thanks to @Ibrahim4594). `detect` stays small on a page that floods the console (thanks to @ayagmar) and no longer crashes on a percent sign before a non-ASCII character (thanks to @Mercury-nju). Comps, review captures and critique snapshots stay out of git, and `init` says which files to commit (thanks to @probablykabari). New work asks before replacing an existing DESIGN.md (thanks to @MrMuzik), and a decision page left in a background tab no longer reads as closed (thanks to @connerohnesorge). Claude Code gets its own short skill description that fits its skill list.

name: CLI 4.8.1
body:
- **ES module sources.** `detect <dir>` now scans `.mjs` and `.cjs` files, which it already checked when you named them one at a time.

- **Steadier scans.** A page that floods the browser with console or network events no longer grows the process without bound, and a percent escape before a non-ASCII character no longer crashes `detect`.

- **Install does what you pick.** A harness chosen in the interactive picker installs even when another one is already there, and the success line names every hook file it wrote.

- **Accurate update checks on Windows.** `check` no longer reports an update on every Windows install.

- **The current detector.** Engine 0.1.19 brings the contrast and background fixes in skill v4.8.1.
